title: Chasing a probe around a cycle
sub: Chandy-Misra-Haas deadlock detection on a five-process wait-for graph.

frames.caption: A wait-for graph: an arrow P1 → P2 means P1 is blocked waiting for a resource P2 holds. P1 to P4 wait on each other in a ring; P5 waits on P3 but nobody waits on P5. No process can see the whole graph.

P1 has been blocked for a while and suspects deadlock. It sends a probe (1, 1, 2) to the process it waits for: initiator 1, sender 1, receiver 2. A probe is three integers, whatever the size of the system.
P2 is itself blocked, so it forwards the probe along its own wait-for edge: (1, 2, 3). Each process forwards a given initiator's probe at most once.
P3 forwards to P4. The probe only travels along wait-for edges, so it never visits P5: P5 waits for P3, not the other way round.

P4 waits for P1, so it sends (1, 4, 1). The probe has come back to its initiator: every process on the way was blocked, and waiting in the AND model ends only when a resource is released, so the cycle is real. P1 declares deadlock after 4 probes, one per edge of the cycle. Some process in the cycle (often the youngest) is then aborted to break it.
